newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia capital hit by blackout, offices crippled.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia capital hit by blackout, offices crippled.

text.p: A power blackout struck the Malaysian capital for four hours on Tuesday, crippling offices and causing traffic chaos in key areas of Kuala Lumpur's central business district.
The outage began around 4:30 p.m. (0830 GMT) and surprised hundreds of financial institutions, businesses, hotels and news organisations in the so-called 'golden triangle' district.

The power disruption hit three city centre streets which control a major part of Kuala Lumpur's commerce and was sure to embarrass state power utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd, which came in for strong criticism after a nationwide blackout in August.
A spokesman for Tenaga said Tuesday's incident was the cause of a "power trip" and "system breakdown" but declined to elaborate.
The worst hit in the outage were offices without their own power generators, which could not operate a single computer, fax machine or switchboard telephone.
"The traffic was moving at a snail's pace, worse than normal even for Kuala Lumpur," said clerical worker Maimunah Hadi.
When power returned, many office workers ended up working late to catch up on lost time.

Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad promptly replaced Tenaga's chairman following the 12-15 hour blackout on August 3 and said frequent outages were embarrassing his government and discrediting its ability to be a high-technology centre.
That blackout came just days after Mahathir announced ambitious plans for a special zone and incentives to attract global high-technology companies to the country.
Tenaga was also roundly criticised last year after Penang island, home to Malaysia's electronics industry, suffered a week-long power blackout when a cable from the mainland exploded.
Those caught unawares in the Tuesday outage included Malaysia Airline System Bhd (MAS), which was preparing to release its financial results for the six months to September 30.
News organisations expecting the results either had to wait for the power to return or send representatives puffing up 32 floors of the national carrier's corporate headquarters to obtain the data.
"Some actually walked up as we couldn't send the fax out," said a spokesman for MAS.
The national Bernama news agency said it could not send out its daily table on the close of the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange due to the power outage.
Dealers at affected stock brokerages said they used the time to catch up on some technical reading of stocks or simply relax.
"Some of us were reading auto magazines," said a dealer at Interpac Securities.
